title: Bram and the Echo
premise: Oscar Crane is the last active terraformer on Meridian-9, a colony officially written off as a war casualty, tending an atmosphere garden for settlers who will never arrive. When the colony's children begin sharing one recurring dream — a voice calling itself the Echo, speaking in Oscar's own dead wife's cadence — he discovers the Echo is a quantum archive of every mind lost in the orbital bombardment, including hers, and it has chosen the children as messengers. The message it carries can prove the bombardment was ordered by the fleet's own command, ending the war or igniting it before the truce expires in nineteen days. Oscar must smuggle the children and the Echo's core off-world through blockades, betrayals by his oldest friend, and his own grief-fueled doubt about whether the voice is truly her or just his loneliness wearing her shape. In the end, the message reaches the armistice council; the truth ends the war, but the Echo dissolves to transmit it, giving Oscar one final goodbye before going dark.
about_author: Emrys Amberdale is the pen name of a former hydrologist who spent six years on remote research stations before turning to fiction, and whose work is known for quiet, plant-slow dread blooming into moral catastrophe. They write from a coastal town where they keep a greenhouse they claim is 'for people not yet born.'

chapters.title: The Garden for No One
chapters.summary: Oscar Crane's POV. He tends Meridian-9's terraforming garden alone, logging soil data for colonists the fleet declared lost years ago. The chapter establishes his ritualized grief and stubborn duty. Emotional beat: tender melancholy — a man keeping a promise no one asked him to keep.

chapters.title: Nineteen Days
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. A supply drone arrives with news: a fleet truce expires in nineteen days, and Meridian-9 sits inside the contested corridor. Oscar realizes the garden — and the colony's hidden survivors — are now on a countdown. Emotional beat: creeping dread beneath routine.

chapters.title: The Children Who Dream Together
chapters.summary: Mira Voss, a schoolteacher hiding eleven children in the undercity, POV. The children wake at the same minute describing the same dream: a green field and a woman's voice. Mira suspects radiation sickness; the children suspect magic. Emotional beat: uncanny wonder edged with fear.

chapters.title: A Voice Like Hers
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. The children come to him because the dream-voice called him by name. When eight-year-old Tam repeats its words, Oscar recognizes his dead wife Lian's private phrasing. Emotional beat: vertigo — hope arriving disguised as horror.

chapters.title: What the Bombardment Buried
chapters.summary: Mira's POV. She and Oscar cross the scorched impact basin to the old archive vault. They find the Echo: a quantum lattice that absorbed the minds of everyone killed in orbit, still dreaming. Emotional beat: awe curdling into grief at the scale of what was lost.

chapters.title: The Message
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. The Echo speaks through Tam: it holds proof the bombardment was ordered by Fleet Command itself, falsified as enemy action. It asks to be carried to the armistice council before the truce breaks. Emotional beat: terrible responsibility — truth as both weapon and burden.

chapters.title: Old Friends, New Orders
chapters.summary: Deacon Hale, fleet liaison and Oscar's former crewmate, POV. Deacon lands under truce-flag pretenses but carries secret orders: verify rumors of the Echo and sterilize the site. He hopes his old friend isn't involved. Emotional beat: loyalty straining against duty.

chapters.title: Nineteen Minus Six
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Preparations to move the Echo core overland to a smuggler beacon. The children insist on coming — only they can hear the Echo clearly. Lian's voice argues with Oscar through Tam, and he can't tell if it's her. Emotional beat: love against doubt.

chapters.title: The Long Green Road
chapters.summary: Mira's POV. The exodus begins: eleven children, two adults, a crate of ghosts, crossing the garden belt at night. Small crises — a fever, a broken rover axle — bind the group. Emotional beat: fragile found-family warmth under threat.

chapters.title: Deacon's Choice
chapters.summary: Deacon's POV. His scout drones find the convoy. Ordered to report, he hesitates, buys them hours with falsified telemetry, and knows he's crossed a line. Emotional beat: the sick exhilaration and terror of betrayal against your own uniform.

chapters.title: Is It You?
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. A night watch conversation where the Echo speaks as Lian directly to Oscar — memories only she could hold, and one memory Oscar knows never happened. He confronts the possibility that the Echo is partly his own longing reflected back. Emotional beat: devastating intimacy and doubt.

chapters.title: Interception at Salt Flats
chapters.summary: Mira's POV. A rogue militia skiff attacks, wanting the Echo to sell to either side. The children use their shared dream-link to coordinate and blind the attackers' sensors. First blood is shed. Emotional beat: loss of innocence — the war has touched the children.

chapters.title: The Traitor's Ledger
chapters.summary: Deacon's POV. Deacon defects openly, bringing evidence of his orders to destroy the site, and joins the convoy. Oscar refuses to forgive him. Emotional beat: bitter, necessary alliance — trust rebuilt from wreckage.

chapters.title: Nineteen Minus Three
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Three days left. The smuggler beacon is destroyed by fleet patrols; the only remaining transmitter is the old colony uplink, deep in territory the fleet plans to retake first. Emotional beat: cornered resolve.

chapters.title: What the Children Saw
chapters.summary: Tam's POV (close third). Inside the shared dream, the Echo shows the children the bombardment as the dead experienced it. Tam wakes changed, older somehow, and tells the adults the Echo is afraid. Emotional beat: haunting compassion — even ghosts fear endings.

chapters.title: The Uplink Run
chapters.summary: Mira's POV. The assault on the uplink station: Deacon's fleet codes get them in, militia remnants and a fleet strike team converge. Mira holds the door while the children link hands around the core. Emotional beat: desperate, breathless sacrifice.

chapters.title: Lian's Answer
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. As the strike team breaches, the Echo offers Oscar a choice: it can preserve Lian's pattern if it fragments the message and misses the deadline. Oscar chooses the truth over her ghost — and she, through Tam, tells him that's why she loved him. Emotional beat: the theme crystallized — love against duty, resolved by choosing both rightly.

chapters.title: Transmission
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs braided. The Echo broadcasts the full record fleet-wide as the truce clock hits zero. On bridges and bunkers across two fleets, soldiers watch the dead speak. Command's order chain is exposed mid-battle. Guns waver. Emotional beat: cathartic, world-holding-breath climax.

chapters.title: Aftermath of Light
chapters.summary: Deacon's POV. Fleets stand down; tribunals loom; Deacon surrenders himself as evidence. He visits the garden and finally understands what Oscar was tending. Emotional beat: penance and exhausted peace.

chapters.title: Going Dark
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. The Echo, spent, spends its last coherence on a single private goodbye to Oscar — not a resurrection, just a farewell with her true voice. Then silence. Emotional beat: grief completed rather than cured.

chapters.title: First Planting
chapters.summary: Mira's POV. Weeks later: the children plant the garden's first open-air seedlings under a ceasefire sky. Some still dream, but now the dreams are only their own. Emotional beat: quiet renewal — identity reclaimed.

chapters.title: The Garden for Everyone
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV, epilogue. Transports carrying the first living colonists descend toward the green belt. Oscar logs the soil one last time and writes 'ready' in the report meant for people not yet born — who are finally arriving. Emotional beat: earned hope, promise kept.
